knowledge:
- key_parameters: max.probes=Maximum limit of annotated genes allowed for a term of interest to be analyzed (terms exceeding this are skipped) ;; B=Number of random samplings used to compute empirical p-values ;; return.cut=Logical indicating whether diana2means should return the split classifications and score (TRUE) or just the score (FALSE) ;; ignore.genes=Number of top-scoring genes to exclude from DLD-score calculation to prevent single highly variable genes from dominating the score ;; filter.fdr=FDR threshold used to filter and display significant splits in the image plot
- alternatives: Standard k-means clustering with random initialization (diana2means is preferred as its hierarchical centroid initialization outperforms random starting points) ;; ISIS package (from which the DLD-score implementation is derived)
- when_to_use: Use this package when you want to perform unsupervised class discovery on patient/sample expression profiles using biologically focused gene sets (defined by GO terms or KEGG pathways) rather than all genes, allowing you to identify and functionally characterize distinct patient subgroups.
- pitfalls: Terms with too many associated probesets (e.g., generic GO terms) or too few probesets will be automatically skipped unless max.probes is adjusted ;; Single highly variable genes can disproportionately drive the DLD-score, which can be mitigated by setting ignore.genes ;; Multiple testing is a major issue when testing many pathways, requiring FDR correction (q-values) which is automatically computed but requires a sufficiently high number of permutations (B).

workflows.name: annotation_driven_clustering
workflows.intent: Perform annotation-driven class discovery on expression data using GO/KEGG annotations, compute empirical significance, and visualize the resulting patient splits.
input: Character string (name of the Bioconductor chip-specific annotation metadata package)
workflows.stages: 1. Run adSplit to generate splits for specific terms or entire ontologies ("GO", "KEGG", "all") with permutation testing to compute empirical p-values. ;; 2. Summarize the resulting splitSet object. ;; 3. Plot a histogram of empirical p-values and corrected q-values. ;; 4. Generate a clustered heatmap image of the significant splits filtered by FDR.
workflows.code:
library(adSplit)
library(golubEsets)
data(Golub_Merge)
glutamSplits <- adSplit(Golub_Merge, "KEGG:00251", "hu6800", B=1000)
print(glutamSplits)
x <- adSplit(Golub_Merge, c("GO:0007165","GO:0006915"), "hu6800", max.probes=7000)
print(x)
x <- adSplit(Golub_Merge, "KEGG", "hu6800")
print(x)
data(golubKEGGSplits)
print(golubKEGGSplits)
summary(golubKEGGSplits$qvalues)
hist(golubKEGGSplits)
image(golubKEGGSplits, filter.fdr=0.3, outfile="splitSet.eps", res=300)

workflows.name: manual_split_and_null_distribution
workflows.intent: Manually cluster samples using divisive hierarchical 2-means on a custom gene subset and generate a null distribution of DLD-scores using random gene sets.
input: Matrix (gene expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
Environment (Entrez ID to probe set mapping environment from chip metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter the expression matrix for highly variable genes. ;; 2. Run diana2means to cluster samples and retrieve the split classifications and DLD-score. ;; 3. Create an Entrez ID to probe set environment using makeEID2PROBESenv. ;; 4. Draw random probe sets using drawRandomPS. ;; 5. Generate a null distribution of DLD-scores using randomDiana2means and plot the distributions.
workflows.code:
library(adSplit)
library(golubEsets)
data(Golub_Merge)
e <- exprs(Golub_Merge)
vars <- apply(e, 1, var)
e <- e[vars > quantile(vars,0.9),]
diana2means(e)
diana2means(e, return.cut=TRUE)
x <- diana2means(e, return.cut=TRUE)
x$cut
EID2PSenv <- makeEID2PROBESenv(hu6800ENTREZID)
drawRandomPS(10, EID2PSenv, ls(EID2PSenv))
scores <- randomDiana2means(20, exprs(Golub_Merge), "hu6800", ndraws = 1000)
scores2 <- randomDiana2means(20, exprs(Golub_Merge), "hu6800", ndraws = 1000, ignore.genes=5)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
hist(scores,  nclass=30, main="", col="grey")
hist(scores2, nclass=30, main="", col="grey")
